title: Annotator Ops — Incident Response, Escrow & Quality Containment Procedure
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary:
This playbook documents the operational procedure for annotation workforce incidents that threaten eval integrity or production-quality guardrails. It covers detection signals, immediate containment steps, escrowing of contested annotation assets, short-term remediation, and post-incident review requirements. The goal is to preserve evaluation provenance, minimize label corruption, and restore trustworthy evaluator/annotator state within defined SLOs.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to: in-house annotators, managed third-party vendors, and contractor annotator pools used for probes, prompts, and gold labels associated with evaluation assets.
- Not in scope: model training data acquisition pipelines (separate data governance policy), provider-only telemetry incidents that never touch human labels.

Definitions:
- Contested asset: any probe, prompt, or annotation bundle suspected of compromise (e.g., sudden label drift, coordinated low-agreement).
- Escrow: a write-once, access-controlled snapshot of contested assets and associated metadata (annotator ids, timestamps, session logs).
- Quarantine cohort: subset of annotators or probes suspended from routing while investigation occurs.

Roles and responsibilities:
- Incident Lead (IL) — typically the applied-ml oncall or annotation steward. Owns containment, escalation, and sign-off.
- Annotation Steward — operational owner for the annotator pool; responsible for escrow snapshot and vendor coordination.
- Quality SME — product/ML engineer who assesses quality impact and approves remediation.
- Security Liaison — engages if there is suspected malicious activity or PII leakage.
- Legal/Compliance — engaged for regulatory incidents or customer-sensitive content.

Detection signals (examples):
1) Sudden drop in inter-annotator agreement (IAA) for a probe family: >= 15 percentage points relative to 7-day rolling baseline.
2) Spike in label entropy or label-flip rate: > 3x normal for same slice.
3) Anomalous annotator session behavior: >= 4 short sessions (< 2 minutes) followed by many identical labels.
4) External report: customer or internal reviewer flags consistent mislabeling on high-sensitivity probes.

Immediate containment checklist (TL;DR for first 30 minutes):
1. Triage: IL declares an annotation integrity incident and sets severity (Critical | High | Medium | Low).
2. Quarantine: stop routing new assignments to suspect annotators / vendor cohort and mark related probes as contested.
3. Escrow snapshot: create a timestamped, immutable export of contested assets and session logs (see Escrow procedure).
4. Notify: page Quality SME and Security Liaison if PII or malicious indicators are present.
5. Communication: update an incident thread in the eval-ops channel and record short summary in the incident tracker.

Escrow procedure (runnable steps):
- Precondition: annotator telemetry retention must include session_id, worker_id (pseudonymized), assignment_id, start/end timestamps, and raw label payload.
- CLI snapshot example (internal tooling):
```
# create escrow bundle for probe-family "account-auth" between timestamps
eval-escrow create --probe-family account-auth --from 2026-06-01T00:00:00Z --to 2026-06-01T06:00:00Z --output /escrow/2026-06-01-account-auth.tar.gz
eval-escrow attest --bundle /escrow/2026-06-01-account-auth.tar.gz --owner maya.chen@redwood.ai
```
- Access control: escrow bundles are stored in S3 bucket redwood-escrow-{env}, encrypted with KMS key arn:aws:kms:region:acct:key/escrow. Access requires IL + Annotation Steward approval in the access request system.
- Retention: contested escrow bundles are retained for 180 days by default; longer retention requires Legal approval.

Containment decision matrix (where to route probes during incident):
| Severity | Immediate routing behavior | Notes |
| Critical | Pause all related probe traffic to hosted eval mesh | Only synthetic can continue for unaffected families |
| High | Route to shadow-only (no production scoring) | Enables triage without production impact |
| Medium | Reduce sampling rate by 90% and flag outputs | Conservative approach for borderline cases |
| Low | Continue with increased monitoring | Alert Quality SME for manual checks |

Triage investigation steps (hour 0–6):
1. Recompute slice-level metrics (IAA, label entropy, repeat-label frequency) for contested assets.
2. Compare session fingerprints against baseline: IP geography, browser agent, session cadence.
3. Re-annotate a 5–10% stratified random sample with trusted annotators (blind duplication) to estimate contamination.
4. If contamination > 10% of sample, escalate to Remediation; otherwise close as false alarm with notes.

Remediation playbook (when contamination confirmed):
1. Rollback and scrub: remove contested labels from active evals and flag impacted results.
2. Re-annotation: schedule re-labeling with trusted annotator cohort; use double-blind consensus (N=3) for high-sensitivity slices.
3. Quarantine annotators: disable accounts and preserve telemetry for forensics.
4. Vendor action: if vendor-managed, move to contractual remediation path and apply holdback clauses as required.
5. Model/Metric impact: recompute key eval metrics and publish delta report to stakeholders.

Quality SLOs and thresholds (operational targets):
- Detection SLA: Contested-signal alert acknowledged by IL within 30 minutes in 90% of incidents.
- Containment SLA: Quarantine and escrow snapshot completed within 60 minutes for Critical/High incidents.
- Resolution SLA: Re-annotation workflow started within 72 hours for impacted high-sensitivity probes.
- Root-cause review: Post-incident review published within 7 calendar days.

Forensic artifacts and mandatory evidence set (for every incident):
- Escrow bundle (labels, session metadata, assignment traces)
- Snapshot of eval-mesh requests/response logs correlated by probe_id
- Annotator roster snapshot and policy state at incident time
- Re-annotation sample results and reconciliation notes
- Communication log and approvals for access to escrow

Communication checklist (stakeholder cadence):
- T+0 (initial): short incident page and triage classification to eval-ops channel and IL pager.
- T+6 (status): preliminary contamination estimate and containment actions to product and ML lead.
- T+72 (remediation start): plan for reannotation and expected customer-facing impact.
- T+7 (postmortem): published RCA and action items.

Post-incident review template (minimum sections):
1. Executive summary
2. Timeline of detection → containment → remediation
3. Root cause analysis (human error / tooling / vendor / adversarial)
4. Evidence bundles (links to escrow and forensic logs)
5. Cost and coverage impact (probe counts, affected evals, annotated hours)
6. Action items (owners, deadlines, verification criteria)
7. Preventative controls to be implemented (triage automation, sampling rules, SLA changes)

Preventative controls (recommended):
- Active telemetry fuzzing: randomized blind checks routed to internal trusted annotators at a 0.5% sampling rate.
- Agreement sentinel triggers: automatic incident creation when IAA delta > 12 pts for a probe family.
- Vendor audit clause: quarterly quality attestations and a minimum double-annotation rate for sensitive slices.
- Annotator identity hygiene: pseudonymization + rotating worker identifiers to reduce targeted collusion risk.

Operational runbook snippets (automation examples):
- Auto-create incident when metric crosses threshold (pseudo-DSL):
```
on metric("probe.IAA.delta") > 12 pts for 1h -> create incident(type=annotation-integrity) -> attach telemetry bundle
```
- Reannotation workflow kickoff (HTTP API):
POST /internal/reannotation/start
Body: {"probe_family":"account-auth","sample_size":250,"consensus_policy":"n=3-majority"}

Audit and compliance notes:
- Any incident affecting customer-sourced probes must notify Legal within 24 hours.
- Retention of escrow bundles for customer-impacting incidents extends to 7 years if requested by Legal/Compliance.

Open questions and future work:
- Automated label provenance hashing for faster integrity checks (prototype Q3 2026).
- Standard vendor SLAs for annotation speed vs. double-annotation guarantees.

Appendix A — Example incident timeline (illustrative):
- 10:03 UTC: monitoring alert triggered (IAA delta = 18).
- 10:07 UTC: IL acknowledged, quarantined vendor cohort, paused probe routing.
- 10:25 UTC: escrow bundle created and attested.
- 13:00 UTC: re-annotation pilot of 200 items with trusted cohort; contamination = 14%.
- 14:30 UTC: remediation plan approved; re-annotation scheduled, vendor contract notified.
- 2026-03-22: Postmortem published with action items to add sentinel-based auto-triage.

Appendix B — Example evidence JSON schema (for tooling integration):
{
  "probe_id":"string",
  "bundle_id":"string",
  "captured_at":"ISO-8601 timestamp",
  "annotator_ids":["pseud-1","pseud-2"],
  "raw_labels":"base64 or path to object store"
}
